paper_title: WaFFLe: Gated Cache-Ways with Per-Core Fine-Grained DVFS for Reduced On-Chip Temperature and Leakage Consumption

extraction.paper_title: WaFFLe: Gated Cache-Ways with Per-core Fine-grained DVFS for Reduced On-chip Temperature and Leakage Consumption

scenario.figure_or_table: Table 3 (with Table 1, Fig. 13, Fig. 16 and Fig. 29)
scenario.description: Selected scenario: WaFFLe combined cache-way shutdown plus stall-induced fine-grained DVFS on a 16-core homogeneous tiled CMP with an 8MB LLC, compared against baseline, GDP1 and GDP2. Paper-reported thermal observables are peak temperature reduction 8.4 C and average temperature reduction 6.2 C, with IPS degradation 2.5%. No block-level geometry or per-block power table is published in the packet text, and no linked assets were found.
scenario.architecture: 16-tile homogeneous 2D tiled CMP: Alpha 21364 OoO cores, 64KB 4-way L1-I and L1-D, distributed shared 16-way SNUCA L2 banks (1MB per bank in the analysis; 8MB total LLC in the Table 3 comparison), 2D mesh NoC, per-core on-chip voltage regulators, 32nm technology, ambient 47 C
scenario.workload: Multi-threaded PARSEC benchmarks (nine applications, large input sets, 16 threads, RoI portion), all cores always active
scenario.operating_point: Max V/F 1.12V/3.0GHz, min V/F 0.76V/1.2GHz, 70ns DRAM latency, 0.33us thermal interval, 2M-cycle way-shutdown interval, POWER_UP=0.04, POWER_DOWN=0.025

original_setup.solver: Coupled gem5 full-system (Ruby) performance simulation, McPAT 32nm dynamic power and area, per-component temperature-dependent leakage recomputed each interval, and HotSpot 6.0 with HotFloorPlan-generated floorplan. Interval is 0.33 us, with temperature assumed stable within it.
original_setup.optimizer: No formal optimizer. Threshold heuristics set by design-time tuning: POWER_UP=0.04, POWER_DOWN=0.025, a 2M-cycle interval, and a WayLimit cap on gated ways.
original_setup.controller: WaFFLe: (1) Algorithm 1, per-bank miss-ratio-driven LLC cache-way power gating that moves clean non-MRU victim data; (2) Algorithm 2, per-core fine-grained DVFS between 1.12V/3.0GHz and 0.76V/1.2GHz, triggered by global isolated LLC misses detected in the LLC directory.
original_setup.benchmark: Nine multi-threaded PARSEC applications (large inputs, 16 threads, RoI), 16-tile Alpha 21364 OoO CMP, 8MB LLC, 32nm, 47 C ambient. Compared against the baseline and the prior GDP1 and GDP2 policies (Table 3).

thermal_observable.unit: degC (reduction in peak temperature versus baseline)
thermal_observable.location: Chip-wide peak temperature across all on-chip components of the 16-core CMP (cores and L2 banks, HotSpot block-level), 8MB LLC configuration
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum reduction in peak chip temperature over the nine PARSEC applications, WaFFLe versus baseline. The paper also reports a 6.2 degC maximum reduction in average chip temperature and 2.5% average IPS degradation.

physical_mismatches.reason: WaFFLe is a runtime transient controller. Cache ways are gated on and off every 2M cycles, and per-core DVFS reacts to memory stalls within about 70 ns. The reported temperature reductions come from time-varying power traces at 0.33 us. A static floorplan with fixed block power cannot represent this controller or its reported gains.

Power depends on the coupled gem5/McPAT performance simulation: workload phases, miss ratios, stall periods, and V/F switching. Leakage is recomputed from per-component temperature feedback. Studio would need equivalent time-resolved per-block power, which the paper does not publish.

The observable is a reduction relative to a baseline across PARSEC workloads, produced by dynamic cache-way gating and DVFS that change power per block. No scenario with fixed published geometry and per-block power reproduces it.

The packet publishes no block-level geometry, no per-block power table, and no HotSpot package or material parameters. Fig. 16 and Fig. 20 show floorplan labels and temperatures only, not coordinates or powers.
The setup is 2D with no 3D stacking or interposer, so no 3D mismatch arises. Cooling and package details such as heat sink and TIM are unspecified, so a cooling mismatch cannot be ruled out.
The LLC size is ambiguous. Table 1 gives 1MB 16-way L2 per tile, which implies 16MB across 16 tiles, while the Table 3 comparison and Sec. 5.1 use an 8MB LLC.

methods.note: Sec. 4 (pp. 12-13) confirms the coupled gem5 (Ruby) + McPAT 32nm + per-component leakage recomputation + HotSpot 6.0/HotFloorPlan flow at a 0.33 us interval. Algorithms 1 and 2 (pp. 6, 11) match the controller description. The packet is text-only, so the figures were not visually verified. The extraction's classification of the setup as dynamic/transient is supported by the text. Inferred statements, such as the aggregation of the Table 3 values as a maximum over applications, rest on p. 15 prose, not on the table itself.

code.note: No code, repository, availability statement or supplementary link was found in the supplied text, and the assets list is empty. The extraction's 'checked_no_links' rests on a pdftotext scan only, which cannot rule out links lost in layout or figures. No code can be verified.

parameters.note: Table 1 (p. 13), 1.12V/3.0GHz and 0.76V/1.2GHz, 70 ns DRAM latency, 0.33 us and 2M-cycle intervals, POWER_UP 0.04, POWER_DOWN 0.025 and the regulator powers 0.106/0.168 W (p. 14) all match the text. However, the WayLimit value, which is decisive for the maximum LLC shrinkage and therefore for the gains, is never given and the extraction does not list it as missing. The 8MB LLC conflicts with Table 1 and the Fig. 2-5 captions (1MB 16-way per bank x 16 tiles = 16MB); the paper does not resolve this, and the 16MB sensitivity result in Fig. 23b (10.5-12 C) differs from the 8.4 C headline.

config.note: HotSpot package, die/thickness, TIM, spreader, heat sink and convection parameters, and material properties are not published, and the HotFloorPlan area inputs are not given. Only a 47 C ambient (p. 13, Table 1) is given. Any reproduction would have to assume the cooling stack. The extraction's 'experiment' field is kind custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and power. This contradicts its own steady_2d_relevant=false and its essential mismatches, so no valid scenario configuration exists.

data.note: Table 3 (p. 22) reductions of 8.4/6.2 C and 2.5% IPS degradation, plus the GDP1/GDP2 values, are correctly transcribed from the page text. No per-block floorplan coordinates or per-block power exist for the baseline or WaFFLe 8MB scenario, so no same-scenario power can exist for any floorplan block. Fig. 16, 17, 20 and 29, the figures behind the observable, were not available as images, so no decisive figure was visually verified. Fig. 16/20 show labels and temperatures that appear to be in Kelvin (e.g. 373.83 vs 366.59), which the extraction does not note.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and the gate blocked the run (simulation_allowed=false, comparison_valid=false). Studio did not run: simulation status is 'skipped' because the custom experiment has no floorplan blocks and no power_w object, so there is no Studio output. The scenario is WaFFLe (gated LLC ways plus per-core fine-grained DVFS) on a 16-core tiled CMP with an 8MB LLC. The paper reports a peak temperature reduction of 8.4 C, an average temperature reduction of 6.2 C and 2.5% IPS degradation versus baseline, with GDP1 at 6.1 C and GDP2 at 6.7 C peak reduction. These are maximum reductions over nine PARSEC applications from a coupled gem5/McPAT/HotSpot transient simulation at 0.33 us intervals. The experiment was labeled custom_2d_steady, which has no transient trace, and cannot represent a runtime controller whose gains come from time-varying power. No numerical comparison with Studio is made or valid, since the location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions do not match and no Studio result exists. Qualitatively, lowering power in cores and cache banks should lower temperature, but that is a general expectation and not a replication or validation of the 8.4 C figure. The final verdict is that the paper is not reproducible in Studio from the packet. The independent page/asset review and the adversarial checks are also unresolved, so none of the extracted evidence is independently verified.
